newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO plunges, shruggs off stock draw.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO plunges, shruggs off stock draw.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil's downtrend remained intact with aggressive selling, while bids were scarce, traders said on Thursday.
Sellers were undercutting one another against no firm buyers, a trader said.
Three offers were heard between $109-$113 per tonne for late January to early February loading supplies, traders said. This compared with Wednesday's $113.00/$115.00.
"Offers are edging down by the minute without any buying support," said a trader.
Latest figures released by the Trade Developement Board of Singapore showed a fall of 926,000 barrels in residue stocks, but the decline did not provide support, traders said.
Taiwan has awarded its tender to buy two cargoes of 38,000 tonnes of fuel oil for loading in February at $136-$138 per tonne dwon from its previous award for January supplies at $149 per tonne.
Traders said weak fundamantals were here to stay for the prompt loading dates.
January fuel oil swaps was last quoted at $111.00/$112.00, down from Wednesday's $112.00, in line with the softer physical market.
